In the reported scenario the cart items list is [mug (2×12.50=25.00), lamp (39.99), pen (3×1.00=3.00)]; the loop sums only items[0] and items[1] = 25.00 + 39.99 = 64.99, dropping the pens line entirely — exactly the reported value, and exactly $3.00 short of the correct 67.99. No bulk discount applies (tiers start at 10+ units per README), so 67.99 is correct. The defect is the off-by-one in the loop, not in add(), LineItem.total, or order_total.

payload.root_cause: Cart.subtotal() in pyshop/cart.py uses `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1)`, an off-by-one that iterates only indices 0..N-2 and excludes the last line item from the sum. With 3 distinct products (mug line 25.00, lamp line 39.99, pen line 3.00) it sums only the first two lines = 64.99 instead of 67.99. Any multi-product cart therefore under-reports its subtotal by the value of the last line; the same wrong subtotal propagates into order_total(). Correct iteration is over all items (e.g. `sum(item.total for item in self.items)`).
evidence: pyshop/cart.py:52-56 — `subtotal()` loops `for i in range(len(self.items) - 1): total += self.items[i].total`, skipping the final line item (off-by-one).

pyshop/cart.py:41-43 — items are appended in insertion order, so the last added product (pens, 3×$1.00 = $3.00) is the one dropped: 25.00 + 39.99 = 64.99, matching the bug report exactly (67.99 − 64.99 = 3.00).

pyshop/cart.py:22-25 — LineItem.total applies bulk_discount_pct, which per docs/README.md is 0% below 10 units, so no discount should alter these three lines; the discrepancy is purely the missing line.
tests/test_cart.py:21-25 — test_subtotal_sums_all_lines expects 67.99 for the exact same cart (2 mugs, 1 lamp, 3 pens), confirming intended behavior.
pyshop/cart.py:69 — order_total() calls cart.subtotal(), so the under-count propagates to discounted subtotal, shipping threshold and tax.
